title: Code for Scene Filtering
body: Thank you for the great repo Are you also planning to release the code to compute scene probabilities scene filtering for a given image I m referring to the module that you mention at Section 3 2 of your paper which is needed to decide which images are kept or discarded for training

comments.body: Thank you for your comment You can find the code for extracting scene probabilities in the original tf https github com TIBHannover GeoEstimation tree original tf branch of the repository specifically in the file scene classification py https github com TIBHannover GeoEstimation blob original tf scene classification py We have not provided the scene classification code for the PyTorch implementation in the master branch However if you prefer a PyTorch version for scene classification we kindly refer you to the Places365 repository https github com CSAILVision places365 We hope this helps you
That was very useful If you want I can submit a PR to port that in pytorch in your repo what do you think

Also what are the differences between the pytorch code and the paper Should each of the dataset s subsets nature indoor urban be passed to a different net so effectively there should be 3 of the models implemented in the code

Thanks a PR would be great of course but please don t feel obligated to do that The pytorch code for the base models should not differ from the paper but has been reimplemented and the models have been retrained thus the results slightly differ We only did not implement the ISNs in PyTorch yet Yes you are correct the ISNs are three networks that are trained separately on images that have a scene probability higher than tau s 0 3 for the respective natural environment nature indoor urban The details can be found in Section 3 3 paragraph Individual Scene Networks ISNs and Section 4 paragraph Scene Classification Parameters We have already extracted the three scene probabilities for each training image You can find them in the file mp16 places365 csv https github com TIBHannover GeoEstimation releases download v1 0 mp16 places365 csv in this release https github com TIBHannover GeoEstimation releases tag v1 0 Also note that we initialized the network with the weights learned by the base model when finetuning an ISN as it saved training time and provided better results During inference the Places365 model predicts the most likely environmental scene and the ISN trained for this respective environment is used for geolocalization However it is also worth noting that we tried different architectures including a more powerful EfficientNet in a follow up paper at WACV 22 https openaccess thecvf com content WACV2022 papers Theiner Interpretable Semantic Photo Geolocation WACV 2022 paper pdf and already achieved better results but we also did not try ISNs You can find the repo here https github com jtheiner semantic geo partitioning tree main geo classification

Thanks for the thorough explanation and the reference I opened a PR to port the scene classification py https github com TIBHannover GeoEstimation blob original tf scene classification py script in pytorch
Thank you very much

title: tf2 branch no scene classification?
body: Hi as I recall from the original branch there is a scene classification step before the geoestimation In the tf2 branch is this gone or integrated into the geoestimation and what would be the reasoning Thanks

comments.body: Hi for simplification we omitted the code for the individual scenery networks ISNs that utilize scene classification in the tf2 branch We decided to provide the base M model as it achieves good results across all scene types and it only required to convert one model If you want to train ISNs yourself follow these steps 1 Prepare three datasets that contain images for natural urban or indoor scenes 2 Train one network per dataset using the code in the tf2 branch 3 During inference predict the scene of the image and use the corresponding ISN for geolocation estimation We hope we were able to help you
Hi thanks for the info Would definitely be useful to have a quick inference How has the accuracy differed from using ISNs
